title: Sort by Absolute Difference from K
statement:
Given a sorted array of N integers and a target K, rearrange the array in non-decreasing order of the **absolute difference** of each element from K.

If two elements have the same absolute difference, maintain them in the order they appear in the original sorted array (stable sort criterion).

Print the rearranged array.

Hint: Find the position of K using binary search, then use a two-pointer merge expanding outward.
constraints:
1 <= N <= 10^5
-10^9 <= A[i] <= 10^9
-10^9 <= K <= 10^9
Array is sorted in non-decreasing order.
inputFormat:
Line 1: two integers N and K.
Line 2: N space-separated integers in non-decreasing order.
outputFormat: N space-separated integers: the array sorted by absolute difference from K.
